thread:
mike: quick heads-up — perf dashboard shows a ~12% p95 increase on host request path starting 03/18 deploy, correlates with kernel-selection roll
olivia: ugh. which part of the host path? parsing, tokenization, or grpc framing?
zach: saw something in traces — more writev syscalls and higher header bytes on some flows
mike: right. top two suspects: we added utf8-normalize in pre-tokenizer and kernel selector started preferring a variant that increases kv cache churn (smaller kv segments)
laura: can you paste the profile? even a tiny snippet helps
mike: attaching quick flame (abbreviated):
```
host_ingress -> parse_request (24%) -> tokenize(18%) -> writev(11%) -> kv_cache.lock(6%)
before deploy: tokenize(12%), writev(6%)
```
olivia: tokenize up 6% is suspicious. normalize step + extra memcpy would explain that
zach: writev doubling could be hpack/header growth causing more fragments. did we change any header metadata in routing
mike: only change was adding X-Model-Variant for kernel routing, small header but repeated per-request. might be triggering HPack table churn
laura: HPack churn + small writev fragments = syscalls increase and kernel scheduling overhead on host
olivia: also KV cache churn — if kernels prefer smaller KV shards, we might evict more often, causing tokenization to re-run some heuristics
mike: i profiled bytes/frame and saw average header bytes up 40% for certain clients. trace id 8a7f... if someone wants to grab full trace
zach: @olivia can you run a quick canary: revert X-Model-Variant header emission and re-run the microbench? should be low risk
olivia: on it. running tiny batch now
eng-bot: deploy canary started by olivia at 2026-03-19 16:12 UTC
laura: also suggest adding a metric for writev count per request and hpacks.table_hits to telemetry so we can correlate without pulling traces
mike: agreed. i'll add a shortterm counter in ingress and a KV eviction counter per-shard
zach: another quick probe — disable utf8-normalize path and run host parse bench. if tokenize drops back then we know
olivia: can run both toggles in parallel: header off + normalize off. timeline ~20m
mike: perfect. if both drop, then layered fix: stop emitting header by default + change kernel selector threshold to prefer larger kv segments for 2 weeks
laura: long term: maybe batch the X-Model-Variant header into routing metadata so it doesn't hit HPack frequently (or use compression)
zach: also check streaming chunk boundaries — I noticed slightly smaller chunk sizes after the change which increases framing overhead for gRPC
mike: noted. adding stream.chunk_size histogram to the probe list
olivia: canary results: tokenize p95 back to baseline when normalize disabled, writev still 1.2x if header on. with header off + normalize off both are baseline
mike: good signal. plan: revert header emission for now (opt-out via routing flag) and rollfix normalize into a lazy step (only for non-ascii payloads)
laura: please add an alert if writev count spikes >2x after roll
mike: will do. i'll open PR for the header opt-out and the lazy normalize patch, link here when ready
olivia: PRs up: r/ingress#422 and r/tokenize#133. rolling patch to prod after CI
eng-bot: patch r/ingress#422 merged by olivia at 2026-03-19 16:44 UTC
zach: after rollback metrics look good. p95 back in line. nice catch
mike: huge thanks. follow-ups: (1) add HPack telemetry, (2) experiment with coalescing small frames in writev path, (3) revisit kernel selector defaults to favor kv hit-rate over micro-latency
laura: i'll file the follow-up RFC for kernel selector tweaks and assign owners
mike: ok closing thread once RFC and two follow-up tickets are created
olivia: tickets: #710 (hpack metrics), #711 (frame coalesce), #712 (kernel selector RFC)
mike: awesome, thanks everyone :thumbsup:
